Compute latent factors from cell group scores using NMF

compute.latent_factors.Rd

Usage

compute.latent_factors(
  scores,
  rank = NULL,
  ranks = 2:15,
  n_boot = 100,
  recovery_thresh = 0.7,
  similarity_thresh = 0.8,
  seed = 123,
  file_name = NULL,
  return = TRUE
)

Arguments

scores

Numeric matrix of size samples x cell groups (signed CCA composite scores).

rank

Integer; number of NMF factors. If NULL (default), chosen among ranks with bootstrap NMF (see Details). If given, the stability of its factors is still computed (stability).

ranks

Candidate ranks when rank = NULL. Default 2:15, limited to the number of cell groups (rank 1 with a single cell group).

n_boot

Integer; number of bootstrap NMF runs per rank. Default 100.

recovery_thresh

Numeric; minimum recovery frequency (proportion of bootstrap runs in which the factor is found) for a factor to be robust. Default 0.7.

similarity_thresh

Numeric; minimum cosine similarity for a bootstrap factor to count as the same factor, and minimum mean similarity for a factor to be robust. Two factors of the same rank more similar than this are considered redundant. Default 0.8. Both thresholds are practical starting points, not universal cutoffs.

seed

Random seed used for the NMF fits and the bootstrap samples. Default 123. The caller's random number generator state is restored when the function returns.

file_name

Optional character suffix for the saved patient-mixture plot.

return

Logical. If TRUE (default), saves the patient-mixture barplot to Results/NMF_patient_mixture_<file_name>.pdf (Results/NMF_patient_mixture.pdf if file_name is NULL), and the stability plot to Results/NMF_rank_stability_<file_name>.pdf: the lowest recovery, lowest mean similarity and highest similarity between factors of each candidate rank (with the thresholds and the selected rank; only when the rank is selected), and the recovery and mean similarity of each factor of the selected rank.

Value

A named list with:

Z

Sample-level NMF factor scores (samples x rank). Non-negative. Each factor (column) sums to 1 over the samples: the size of each factor is in nmf_model$d (the NMF is W %*% diag(d) %*% t(Z)). Tests on one factor at a time do not depend on this scale; to compare factors within a sample, multiply each column by its d, as done for patient_mixture.

W

Weights of the cell groups per factor (cell groups x rank). Non-negative.

nmf_input

The matrix fed to NMF: the positive part of the cell group scores (samples x cell groups). nmf_modelThe RcppML::nmf() model object (includes the scaling vector d). patient_mixtureLong-format data frame of per-sample factor proportions used for the mixture plot: the factor scores multiplied by the size of each factor (nmf_model$d), divided by their sum in each sample. stabilityOne row per factor of the selected rank: recovery (proportion of bootstrap runs in which a matching factor is found, cosine similarity >= similarity_thresh), mean_similarity (mean cosine similarity of the matched bootstrap factors), max_similarity_other (highest cosine similarity with another factor of the same rank: a high value suggests redundancy) and robust (recovery >= recovery_thresh and mean similarity >= similarity_thresh). rank_selectionOne row per candidate rank (NULL if rank is given): the number of robust factors, the lowest recovery and mean similarity of its factors, the highest similarity between two of its factors, and stable_distinct (all factors robust and none redundant).

Decomposes signed CCA composite scores into non-negative latent factors by splitting each score into its positive and negative direction components, then applying Non-negative Matrix Factorization via RcppML (fast C++ backend). Only the positive part of the signed cell group scores is used: max(score, 0), how far the sample is on the active side of the TF module of the cell group (negative scores, on the inactive side, become 0). The factors therefore describe the high-activity direction of the cell groups. The scores must not contain missing values.Rank selection by bootstrap NMF (consensus of the factors across resamples of the patients). The profile of a factor is its column of W (the weights of the cell groups). For each candidate rank:

  1. NMF is fitted on all the samples (reference factors) and on n_boot bootstrap samples of the patients (sampled with replacement);

  2. the factors of each bootstrap run are matched one to one to the reference factors by the cosine similarity of their profiles (most similar pairs first), as NMF factors can come in any order;

  3. each reference factor gets its recovery frequency and mean similarity across runs, and the factors of the rank are compared with each other to detect redundancy (two factors with almost the same profile).

The selected rank is the largest one whose factors are all robust and none redundant: as many factors as the data support reliably (low ranks capture the dominant patterns and are almost always stable, so the smallest stable rank would favour 2). If no rank qualifies, the rank with the most robust factors is used (the smallest in case of ties), with a message; check rank_selection and whether the main factors persist at the neighbouring ranks. data("network.tuto") data("deconv_subgroups.tuto") cell_groups <- construct_cell_groups(network.tuto, deconv_subgroups.tuto) latent <- compute.latent_factors(cell_groups$Cell_groups, n_boot = 20, return = FALSE) head(latent$Z) latent$nmf_model$d # size of each factor latent$rank_selection # stability and redundancy of each candidate rank latent$stability # stability of the factors of the selected rank
